facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that the filings already suffice for covenant and priority work is that they print the financing structure in detail: the maximum leverage test of 4.50x, the leverage-based pricing grid, the guarantee and collateral package, the springing-maturity mechanics and a compliance statement at each reporting date. That case wins only where a described covenant is enough, because the filings state neither the reported leverage ratio nor the lender-defined earnings measure, so headroom cannot be computed without the executed agreement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control risk is moderate and rests with the board, not a sponsor. The Chairman and her immediate family beneficially owned about 30% of the shares at the end of 2025 and directors and executive officers about 31% in February 2026, enough to influence director elections and any merger or asset sale, yet the filings state no dealings with the family beyond compensation and director fees in 2023, 2024 and 2025. With no sponsor there are no sponsor fees, no fund-life pressure and no sponsor support to rely on, so creditors depend on the board's own capital allocation and on the debt covenants. Board independence, committee oversight and the table of principal stockholders sit in the proxy statement, which was not supplied. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder returns are the behaviour that most changes creditor risk. In the first nine months of 2026 the company paid USD 475.0 million for share repurchases and USD 43.4 million in dividends, USD 518.4 million in all, which is 1.65x operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million. That comparison overstates the strain, because operating cash flow bore a USD 364.2 million payment for tax credits bought in 2025 and used mainly against tax on the FanDuel sale; before it, operating cash flow would have been USD 677.6 million and returns 0.77x of it. The shares outstanding fell 6.7% from the end of 2025 to the end of September, and the weighted average share count fell 19.4% from 2023 to 2025, so repurchases are a standing policy rather than a one-off. The board raised the quarterly dividend to USD 0.20 per share from USD 0.18 in February 2026 and added USD 500.0 million to the repurchase authorization in April 2026, leaving USD 387.1 million. Both are discretionary and limited only by restricted-payment terms in the credit facility and the notes, whose capacity the filings do not quantify. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 27–28, 58, 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation A6; calculation A7; calculation A8; calculation A9

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The use of the 2025 stake sale was creditor-friendly, but the effect has partly reversed. The company sold its five percent stake in FanDuel on 2025-07-31 for USD 1,758.0 million and used it to repay USD 1,680.9 million outstanding under the prior credit facility in the third quarter of 2025. The facility has since been redrawn: principal outstanding rose from USD 160.7 million at the end of 2025 to USD 800.9 million at 2026-09-30, a rise of USD 640.2 million, in a period when repurchases, dividends and capital spending exceeded operating cash flow. The deleveraging was real but did not become a lower-leverage policy. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk is diversified by geography but weakening where margins are highest. The company operates 26 properties in 11 states, down from 28 at the end of 2024, and gaming provides 65.8% of revenues. Midwest and South properties produce 53.7% of revenues and 56.7% of segment earnings before corporate expense, up from 53.9% a year earlier, while Las Vegas Locals earnings fell 5.7% to USD 293.8 million and Downtown Las Vegas earnings fell 13.8%. The mix is shifting from Las Vegas Locals, the highest-margin property segment at 45.2% of revenue, toward Midwest and South at 37.2%, and total Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 987.5 million, after corporate expense, is 2.9% lower than a year earlier. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Online earnings are far smaller than online revenue suggests, and they have fallen sharply. The Online segment is 15.7% of revenues but 2.8% of segment earnings, because USD 383.0 million of its USD 474.3 million of revenue is reimbursement of gaming taxes and other costs paid for online partners at no margin. Market access fee revenue fell USD 28.9 million after the FanDuel agreements were terminated and in some cases replaced at lower rates, and management says it expects the lower margins to continue. Online Adjusted EBITDAR fell 45.7% to USD 29.9 million. The stake sale therefore monetised a high-margin income stream that is not being replaced at the same level, although technology revenue rose USD 14.2 million, helped by the Design Works acquisition. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 43, 45, 47, 48; calculation A3; calculation A4; calculation A11

facts.text: Management fee income is a growing but contract-bound earnings stream. facts.text: The debt note lists the same two senior note issues at 2026-09-30 as at 2025-12-31, so no new bonds were issued in 2026. USD 400.0 million of the term loan is drawn, USD 800.0 million is undrawn and can be drawn until 2027-07-01, and its maturity springs to 2027-09-01 unless the USD 1,000.0 million of notes due 2027 are retired or refinanced, which is why all USD 800.9 million drawn is classified as current. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings are eroding faster than revenue, but the third quarter shows stabilisation. Revenue is flat at USD 3,022.2 million for nine months, yet house-adjusted EBITDA on trailing revenue fell from 32.5% in 2024 to 29.6%, as market access fees fell away and the earnings of Las Vegas Locals and Downtown Las Vegas declined 5.7% and 13.8% in nine months. In the third quarter alone total Adjusted EBITDAR was down 0.7%, with Online earnings up 16.0% as the fee change laps, while Downtown Las Vegas fell 20.5% and Las Vegas Locals 5.1%. Operating income fell USD 22.4 million as depreciation rose USD 65.4 million, which does not reduce EBITDA but does reduce earnings available after reinvestment. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing is the main credit event and it falls in one window. USD 1,800.9 million of principal, 66.7% of the total, matures in 2027: the facility at its springing maturity of 2027-09-01 and the notes due 2027-12-01, so all USD 800.9 million drawn is classified as current. Committed availability of USD 1,834.9 million covers it only if the term loan is used: USD 800.0 million is a delayed-draw term loan that can be drawn only until 2027-07-01, and revolver availability of USD 1,034.9 million alone would leave USD 34.9 million after retiring the USD 1,000.0 million notes. The issuer states that availability suffices to retire the notes; doing so lifts the floating-rate share of debt from 29.7% to 66.7% and each 100 bp of interest-rate change would cost USD 18.0 million a year against USD 8.0 million today. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 61, 67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B7; calculation B8

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Interest cover is high but flattered by timing. Trailing cash interest of USD 111.7 million, which gives cover of 9.79x, includes only quarters after the 2025 repayment, when the facility balance was lower than the USD 800.9 million now drawn. Annualising the third-quarter interest expense of USD 32.5 million gives USD 130.0 million and cover of 8.42x, and retiring the 2027 notes with facility draws at 5.1% would lift annual interest to about USD 133.7 million and cover to 8.18x. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Boyd Gaming operates 26 gaming properties in 11 states, the online business Boyd Interactive and, under a management agreement, the Sky River Casino. Gaming is 65.8% of revenue and the filings call most revenue cash-based, which supports short cash cycles; the loyalty programme, Boyd Rewards, links the properties and the online offer. For creditors this supports visibility of cash flow and liquidity preservation in a downturn, while the lack of any disclosed customer concentration or market share leaves refinancing confidence resting on the earnings record. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters: properties compete with other operators in each state and in adjacent states, and expansion by competitors or new openings could reduce volumes. Licensing requirements limit new entrants, but Native American casinos and online operators already compete, and some competitors pay lower or no taxes. Substitutes include online gaming and lotteries; buyer power looks high because customers can choose among nearby casinos and the filings describe loyalty rewards as the retention tool; supplier power is not a stated credit factor. The net effect is limited pricing power and margin pressure rather than a collapse in volumes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 27

spans.text: # Boyd Gaming Corp (byd-906553): source readiness as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Boyd Gaming Corp (issuer byd-906553), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This review judges whether the five supplied Boyd Gaming Corporation filings can support the requested analyses of financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit, and records what is missing. It makes no credit conclusion.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Boyd Gaming filings are enough to support a credit snapshot of the consolidated company through the September 30, 2026 quarter, but not covenant headroom, legal priority or rating context, which remain open for creditors.

The latest filing is dated 21 days before the as-of date, the statements, debt note and liquidity discussion agree with one another, and a trailing twelve-month view can be built from filed figures. The earliest maturity date for creditors is the September 1, 2027 springing maturity, which moved USD 800.9 million of credit facility borrowings into current maturities while the USD 1,000.0 million senior notes due 2027 remain outstanding.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 21, 69; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C6
Legal, ratings, peer and market questions are conditional on documents the filings only summarise or omit.
### Key findings

Every filing reports Boyd Gaming Corporation on a consolidated basis, with the senior notes guaranteed by certain wholly owned domestic restricted subsidiaries, so debt, earnings and liquidity describe one reporting entity across all periods. No subsidiary-only statements are supplied; each filing carries summarised combined information for the parent and the guarantor group, which is the only separate financial view of that group.

The filings cover fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 with 2025 comparatives, so a trailing twelve-month position to September 30, 2026 can be built from filed figures; a stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed and would have to be derived. The perimeter moved over the period, with 28 wholly owned properties in the 2024 annual report, 27 in the 2025 annual report and 26 after the August 1, 2026 sale of Sam's Town Shreveport, so period comparisons must use the perimeter changes the filings disclose.

The latest debt note lists the credit facility and both senior note issues with principal, rate, issuance costs and carrying value, and the liquidity discussion repeats the same totals, so the debt stack can be read without outside data. Principal totals USD 2,700.9 million at September 30, 2026, of which USD 800.9 million was reclassified to current maturities because the springing maturity applies while the notes due 2027 are neither retired nor refinanced.

No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, although both are listed as exhibits to the 2025 annual report. No credit rating appears in any filing, and no earnings release, lender presentation or management projection was supplied. Legal and covenant questions therefore rest on the issuer's own summaries, and rating context must come from outside the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 154–156

The latest filing states a maximum leverage ratio of 4.50x and that the company was in compliance at September 30, 2026, but it gives neither the reported ratio nor the minimum interest coverage level under the January 2026 agreement; the 2025 annual report stated a minimum of 2.50x under the earlier agreement. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable from the filings.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that the filings already suffice for covenant and priority work is that they print the financing structure in detail: the maximum leverage test of 4.50x, the leverage-based pricing grid, the guarantee and collateral package, the springing-maturity mechanics and a compliance statement at each reporting date. That case wins only where a described covenant is enough, because the filings state neither the reported leverage ratio nor the lender-defined earnings measure, so headroom cannot be computed without the executed agreement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24

Two developments would change this view. Receipt of the amended credit agreement, or an issuer-reported covenant ratio, would make covenant capacity calculable, and retirement of the notes due 2027, or their refinancing with debt that matures late enough, would remove the springing maturity and ease the near-term liquidity question.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 156

spans.text: # Boyd Gaming Corp (byd-906553): financial foundation as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Boyd Gaming Corp (issuer byd-906553), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module extracts and normalises the consolidated financial statements, debt and liquidity of Boyd Gaming Corporation from five filings through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. It makes no credit recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_byd_bgc20241008-10k.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-21 | 6942b68eed41d9a32a2c297d38367800ac4d1613ac80c98e29dc889f10b62410 | Fiscal 2023 balance sheet and debt table; fiscal 2024 statements as first reported; availability at 2024-12-31 |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-20 | ed6c93717bd02a6fc0254c0b5179399d3c0fdaf8a5790d541c7941d557bedff9 | Fiscal 2023 to 2025 income statement, cash flow, segment note, balance sheets at 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31, debt note, contractual obligations |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_byd_bgc20260331-10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-30 | 71babd7c7d261b102e5e44085ba6b1b17a8a34121746392f5aa5edc883dc9d0b | Three months to 2026-03-31 statements, balance sheet, debt note and availability |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 84dbf526ebb02ac251128639bb21c83ad7b8c354b5cd4a8cdd3439fee2a04dc6 | Nine months to 2026-09-30 statements, balance sheet, debt note, availability, dividends and subsequent events |
| Module output | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 7c8473eaa37b75ce6dd6322228473b3ab21f4de6e4e4e8b5f7e68d8300c0a7cc | Confirms the five filings, the period coverage and the limits on covenant, legal and rating evidence |
## Findings
### Bottom line
Net leverage is moderate at 2.17x trailing reported EBITDA, but net debt rose USD 685.8 million in nine months and USD 800.9 million of facility debt is now current ahead of the 2027 notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19–21; calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation E3

The rise reflects USD 475.0 million of share repurchases and USD 456.0 million of capital spending against operating cash flow of only USD 313.4 million after USD 364.2 million was paid for 2025 tax credits. Interest is not the pressure: trailing EBITDA of USD 1,094.1 million covers trailing cash interest of USD 111.7 million 9.79x, and the exposure is refinancing the 2027 notes and the springing maturity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 15, 21; calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F7; calculation F10; calculation F11
### Key findings

Net debt rose from USD 1,692.2 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 2,377.9 million at September 30, 2026, so net leverage on trailing reported EBITDA moved from 1.61x to 2.17x and total debt leverage from 1.95x to 2.45x. The year-end 2025 position looked lighter than it was because the USD 1,758.0 million proceeds of the 2025 FanDuel sale had already repaid most of the facility and a USD 371.3 million payable for 2025 tax credits sat in accrued liabilities, outside debt, until it was paid in 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 113; calculation N3; calculation N6; calculation F12; calculation F13; calculation F25; calculation F26

Operating cash flow was USD 313.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 701.4 million a year earlier because USD 364.2 million was paid for the 2025 tax credits; before that payment, operating cash flow would have exceeded capital expenditures of USD 456.0 million, not fallen USD 142.6 million short of them. Buybacks of USD 475.0 million and dividends of USD 43.4 million were paid for alongside USD 625.9 million of net facility borrowings, which is how net debt rose.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 15, 58–59; calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F6; calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F9; calculation F23; calculation F24

Trailing reported EBITDA of USD 1,094.1 million covers trailing cash interest of USD 111.7 million 9.79x, up from 6.96x in fiscal 2025, because the third-quarter 2025 repayment cut interest and every quarter in the trailing figure falls after it. The facility has since grown from USD 160.7 million to USD 800.9 million, so trailing interest understates the current run-rate, and cover would fall if that borrowing is carried for a full year.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 19; calculation E5; calculation F2; calculation F10; calculation F11; calculation F33

Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer prints none: it is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, so fiscal 2025 carries USD 128.4 million of impairments. The issuer's own Adjusted EBITDAR adds back master lease rent, which this module deducts, giving house-adjusted trailing EBITDA of USD 1,209.1 million and net leverage of 1.97x, USD 115.0 million above reported EBITDA. The lender-defined earnings measure and the covenant ratio are not printed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation E2; calculation E4; calculation F14; calculation F15; calculation F28

Cash of USD 297.2 million plus USD 1,834.9 million of contractual availability gives USD 2,132.1 million, but all facility borrowings are current and USD 800.0 million of that availability is a delayed-draw term loan that can be drawn only until July 1, 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 20–21; calculation F16; calculation F17; calculation F18; calculation F34

Maturities are concentrated in 2027, when USD 1,800.9 million falls due: the facility at its September 1, 2027 springing maturity and the USD 1,000.0 million notes due December 1, 2027, against USD 900.0 million in 2031. The issuer states that facility availability is enough to retire the 2027 notes and lift the springing maturity, which would leave net debt unchanged but move USD 1,000.0 million from fixed-rate notes to floating-rate facility borrowings that carried a blended rate of 5.1%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 116–117; calculation F19; calculation F20; calculation F21; calculation F35

Obligations outside the debt figure are large: operating lease liabilities of USD 612.2 million, mostly the master leases whose undiscounted payments were USD 537.1 million at the 2025 year-end, and the Norfolk resort, for which the company expects USD 750.0 million of spending including USD 275.0 million in 2026, to be funded from cash on hand, the credit facility and operating cash flow. Leverage here excludes the lease liabilities, the Norfolk commitment and the small assessment arrangements, which sit on separate lines or outside the balance sheet.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19, 26, 64; calculation F37; calculation F38; calculation F39; calculation F40

In the third quarter the company repurchased shares for USD 163.9 million, sold Sam's Town Shreveport on August 1, 2026 and declared a dividend of USD 0.20 per share; the quarterly report identifies no subsequent event requiring disclosure, and the dividend payable on October 15, 2026 is the only dated post-quarter cash payment it states.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 34, 39; calculation F31; calculation F41
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against concern is that leverage is still modest: net leverage of 2.17x is below the 2.37x of fiscal 2024, trailing interest cover is 9.79x, the issuer states that availability suffices to retire the 2027 notes, and the USD 364.2 million tax-credit payment settled a 2025 purchase. That case wins if buybacks slow and EBITDA holds; it fails if repurchases continue at the 2026 pace, because each USD 100 million of further net debt adds about 0.09x of net leverage on trailing reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation F22; calculation F30

Trailing reported EBITDA is USD 43.0 million higher than in fiscal 2025, but only because impairments were smaller: house-adjusted EBITDA is USD 30.9 million lower, and Las Vegas Locals and Online earned less in the first nine months of 2026 than a year earlier. Weaker operations would change the view faster than the debt structure would.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 38; calculation F30; calculation F36
### Limitations

Reported EBITDA is calculated from operating income and depreciation and amortization because the issuer prints no EBITDA, so it includes impairment charges and project costs that the issuer excludes from its own measure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 143
Trailing figures at March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026 are derived from annual and stub-period statements, not reported, and a statement dash is shown as not supplied rather than zero.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation E3
Debt is at carrying value and excludes operating lease liabilities, which the issuer carries on separate lines, so leverage here is not a lease-adjusted measure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 19

spans.text: # Boyd Gaming Corp (byd-906553): business and governance as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Boyd Gaming Corp (issuer byd-906553), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module records what the five supplied filings state about the business, ownership, governance, transactions and capital allocation of Boyd Gaming Corporation and assesses the governance risk they pose to creditors. It makes no credit recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_byd_bgc20241008-10k.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-21 | 6942b68eed41d9a32a2c297d38367800ac4d1613ac80c98e29dc889f10b62410 | First report of the evidence window: 28 properties at 2024-12-31, the Norfolk agreements of 2024-10-21 and the 2023 and 2024 comparatives |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-20 | ed6c93717bd02a6fc0254c0b5179399d3c0fdaf8a5790d541c7941d557bedff9 | Business description, ownership, related-party note, holders of record, audit report, executive officers, subsequent events, the FanDuel stake sale and the 2025 comparatives |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_byd_bgc20260331-10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-30 | 71babd7c7d261b102e5e44085ba6b1b17a8a34121746392f5aa5edc883dc9d0b | Eastside Cannery implosion, Jokers Wild demolition, Design Works agreement and first-quarter segment results |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_byd_bgc20260602-10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-30 | ab14d3952c9150af5e810bed6b7bad085f82cd8a75b40b5982af7951d70e57ac | Repurchase authorization increase of 2026-04-08, Norfolk option exercise of 2026-06-01 and six-month segment results |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-28 | 84dbf526ebb02ac251128639bb21c83ad7b8c354b5cd4a8cdd3439fee2a04dc6 | Latest filing: debt note, commitments and contingencies, repurchase and dividend tables, segment results, capital spending plan, property changes and controls |
| Module output | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 7c8473eaa37b75ce6dd6322228473b3ab21f4de6e4e4e8b5f7e68d8300c0a7cc | Confirms the five filings, the period coverage and that the proxy statement, executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk to creditors is medium: no sponsor and an unqualified audit, but a family-influenced board returned more cash to shareholders in the first nine months of 2026 than operations generated, and the filings do not show the covenant room left.

The consequence is a credit whose protection rests on board restraint and on restricted-payment limits that cannot be tested here. Shareholder returns of USD 518.4 million, made up of USD 475.0 million of repurchases and USD 43.4 million of dividends, were 1.65x operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million, which a USD 364.2 million tax-credit payment had reduced, while the USD 1,758.0 million sale of the FanDuel stake in 2025 first repaid the credit facility. Business risk is moderate: 26 properties in 11 states, with earnings tilting toward Midwest and South properties as Las Vegas locals and online earnings fall.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 24–28, 45, 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 34, 79, 145; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A6; calculation A7
### Key findings

Control risk is moderate and rests with the board, not a sponsor. The Chairman and her immediate family beneficially owned about 30% of the shares at the end of 2025 and directors and executive officers about 31% in February 2026, enough to influence director elections and any merger or asset sale, yet the filings state no dealings with the family beyond compensation and director fees in 2023, 2024 and 2025. With no sponsor there are no sponsor fees, no fund-life pressure and no sponsor support to rely on, so creditors depend on the board's own capital allocation and on the debt covenants. Board independence, committee oversight and the table of principal stockholders sit in the proxy statement, which was not supplied.

Shareholder returns are the behaviour that most changes creditor risk. In the first nine months of 2026 the company paid USD 475.0 million for share repurchases and USD 43.4 million in dividends, USD 518.4 million in all, which is 1.65x operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million. That comparison overstates the strain, because operating cash flow bore a USD 364.2 million payment for tax credits bought in 2025 and used mainly against tax on the FanDuel sale; before it, operating cash flow would have been USD 677.6 million and returns 0.77x of it. The shares outstanding fell 6.7% from the end of 2025 to the end of September, and the weighted average share count fell 19.4% from 2023 to 2025, so repurchases are a standing policy rather than a one-off. The board raised the quarterly dividend to USD 0.20 per share from USD 0.18 in February 2026 and added USD 500.0 million to the repurchase authorization in April 2026, leaving USD 387.1 million. Both are discretionary and limited only by restricted-payment terms in the credit facility and the notes, whose capacity the filings do not quantify.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 27–28, 58, 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation A6; calculation A7; calculation A8; calculation A9

The use of the 2025 stake sale was creditor-friendly, but the effect has partly reversed. The company sold its five percent stake in FanDuel on 2025-07-31 for USD 1,758.0 million and used it to repay USD 1,680.9 million outstanding under the prior credit facility in the third quarter of 2025. The facility has since been redrawn: principal outstanding rose from USD 160.7 million at the end of 2025 to USD 800.9 million at 2026-09-30, a rise of USD 640.2 million, in a period when repurchases, dividends and capital spending exceeded operating cash flow. The deleveraging was real but did not become a lower-leverage policy.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 45; calculation A10

Business risk is diversified by geography but weakening where margins are highest. The company operates 26 properties in 11 states, down from 28 at the end of 2024, and gaming provides 65.8% of revenues. Midwest and South properties produce 53.7% of revenues and 56.7% of segment earnings before corporate expense, up from 53.9% a year earlier, while Las Vegas Locals earnings fell 5.7% to USD 293.8 million and Downtown Las Vegas earnings fell 13.8%. The mix is shifting from Las Vegas Locals, the highest-margin property segment at 45.2% of revenue, toward Midwest and South at 37.2%, and total Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 987.5 million, after corporate expense, is 2.9% lower than a year earlier.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_byd_bgc20241008-10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 45, 48; calculation A3; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A15

Online earnings are far smaller than online revenue suggests, and they have fallen sharply. The Online segment is 15.7% of revenues but 2.8% of segment earnings, because USD 383.0 million of its USD 474.3 million of revenue is reimbursement of gaming taxes and other costs paid for online partners at no margin. Market access fee revenue fell USD 28.9 million after the FanDuel agreements were terminated and in some cases replaced at lower rates, and management says it expects the lower margins to continue. Online Adjusted EBITDAR fell 45.7% to USD 29.9 million. The stake sale therefore monetised a high-margin income stream that is not being replaced at the same level, although technology revenue rose USD 14.2 million, helped by the Design Works acquisition.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 43, 45, 47, 48; calculation A3; calculation A4; calculation A11

Management fee income is a growing but contract-bound earnings stream. The Sky River management fee was USD 82.3 million in nine months, 13.3% higher, and the Managed and Other category contributed 8.4% of segment earnings. The management agreement was signed in 2012 with Wilton Rancheria and runs for seven years from the casino's opening on 2022-08-15, so it ends in 2029 unless extended; the filings state no extension terms. Creditors should treat the income as finite and as dependent on a counterparty that is not part of the borrower group.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 43, 47; calculation A3; calculation A12

Norfolk is the largest single funding and execution commitment. The company expects to spend USD 750.0 million on the project, with USD 275.0 million in 2026, and its management agreement makes it responsible for funding the operating losses of the consolidated entity that holds the license. The transitional casino opened on 2025-11-07 and the full resort is expected to open in November 2027 pending final regulatory approval. The company exercised its option on membership interests of that entity on 2026-06-01 but the filings do not give the percentage. Capital spending of USD 456.0 million in nine months is already 70.2% of the USD 650.0 million planned for 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26, 64; calculation A13

Portfolio actions are small against the balance sheet and show no distress. The company sold Sam's Town Shreveport on 2026-08-01 and the land of the closed Eastside Cannery in the third quarter, received USD 56.8 million from asset sales net of cash transferred in nine months, opened Cadence Crossing on 2026-03-25 to replace Jokers Wild and closed Sam's Town Tunica on 2025-11-09. The acquisition of Design Works for USD 53.3 million closed on 2026-04-01. The pattern is pruning and reinvestment funded from cash and the facility; the filings describe no covenant waiver or lender-driven disposal.

Four properties are leased from a real estate investment trust under master leases, a claim that ranks ahead of the debt in operating cash flow. The leases were extended to 2031-04-30 and master lease rent was USD 86.4 million in nine months. The filings do not state lease coverage, escalators or cross-default terms, so the leases are a fixed charge whose creditor impact cannot be sized from the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 25

Disclosure quality is adequate for monitoring operations but not for testing covenants. The 2025 financial statements carry an unqualified audit opinion with effective internal control and a critical audit matter on goodwill and gaming license impairment, the third-quarter report followed 28 days after the quarter end, and the company states that it complied with its financial covenants. Neither the covenant ratios nor a compliance certificate are printed, and the director, committee and compensation disclosures are incorporated from the unsupplied proxy statement.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 79–81, 149–152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 69; calculation A14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for lower risk is that Boyd Gaming is a widely held public company with an unqualified audit opinion, effective internal control, no dealings with the founding family beyond compensation and director fees, a dividend of only USD 43.4 million in nine months and a stake-sale windfall that first repaid USD 1,680.9 million of facility debt. Repurchases can be stopped at any time, and most of the 2026 cash gap is a one-off tax payment, since returns were 0.91x operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2025. That case wins if repurchases slow once the notes due 2027 are addressed and if the proxy statement confirms an independent board and no related-person transactions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 145–149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 45, 58; calculation A6; calculation A7; calculation A8

The case for higher risk wins if repurchases continue at the 2026 pace while the facility stays drawn, if Norfolk costs exceed USD 750.0 million, or if the credit agreement and indentures show restricted-payment capacity far larger than the USD 387.1 million left under the repurchase authorization. Evidence that would settle the question is the executed credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement, together with the next quarterly report's repurchase figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 63
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, committee oversight, the principal-stockholder table and related-person transactions are not established; independent oversight with no dealings would lower the medium control rating, and material related-party arrangements would raise it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 150–152

- The credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends and repurchase shares is not established; the conclusion on shareholder returns is therefore a judgement about behaviour, not a test of permission, and a capacity much larger than the repurchase authorization would raise the risk.

- Ownership is stated at 2025-12-31 for the family and at 2026-02-16 for directors and officers, and the share count has fallen since, so the current holding is not established and may be higher than the stated percentages.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 2

- The Sky River, Norfolk, master lease and market access agreements are summarised in the notes but were not supplied, so the durability of management fee income and the cost of Norfolk to the borrower rest on summary statements; an extension or a cost overrun would change the judgement on those two items.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26, 47

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The debt note lists the same two senior note issues at 2026-09-30 as at 2025-12-31, so no new bonds were issued in 2026. The only new debt contract is the amended and restated credit agreement signed on 2026-01-21, which replaced the earlier facility with a USD 1,450.0 million revolving credit facility and a USD 1,200.0 million delayed-draw term A loan. USD 400.0 million of the term loan is drawn, USD 800.0 million is undrawn and can be drawn until 2027-07-01, and its maturity springs to 2027-09-01 unless the USD 1,000.0 million of notes due 2027 are retired or refinanced, which is why all USD 800.9 million drawn is classified as current. The facility is secured on substantially all assets other than gaming licenses, carries a maximum net leverage covenant of 4.50x and restricts investments, dividends and other payments.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; calculation A10

The completed transactions are the 2025 sale of the five percent FanDuel stake for USD 1,758.0 million, the 2026-04-01 acquisition of Design Works for USD 53.3 million, the 2026-08-01 sale of Sam's Town Shreveport and the third-quarter sale of the Eastside Cannery land. The stake sale ended a shareholding that had run since 2018 and replaced the strategic partnership with market access agreements at lower fees. None of the completed transactions was financed with new bonds, and the filings state no sale price for Sam's Town Shreveport.

Two commitments remain open: the Norfolk resort, expected to open in November 2027 at a total cost of about USD 750.0 million, and the master leases for four properties, extended to 2031-04-30. The company intends to fund its capital requirements, which include Norfolk, from cash, the credit facility and operating cash flow, and shareholder returns of USD 518.4 million compete with that spending for the same cash. The third-quarter report states that no subsequent event required disclosure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26, 39, 64; calculation A6

## Request

Boyd Gaming Corp (issuer byd-906553), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the five supplied filings and the accepted Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules into a fundamental credit view of Boyd Gaming Corporation. It makes no rating, security or sizing recommendation.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate: net leverage of 2.17x, 2.19x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-10-15, and interest cover of 9.79x are moderate, but shareholder returns have redrawn the credit facility ahead of a concentrated 2027 refinancing.

Earnings are spread across 11 states and committed availability is USD 1,834.9 million, yet operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million in nine months covered neither capital spending of USD 456.0 million nor shareholder returns of USD 518.4 million. The primary downside path is weaker Las Vegas locals earnings with continued repurchases as the springing maturity of 2027-09-01 approaches, which would leave creditors exposed to board policy more than to operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B6
### Key findings

Leverage is moderate but has been rebuilt in 2026. Net leverage on reported EBITDA is 2.17x at 2026-09-30 and 2.19x pro forma for the dividend of USD 14.2 million payable on 2026-10-15, against 1.61x at the end of 2025 and 2.37x at the end of 2024; net debt is USD 2,377.9 million, or USD 2,392.2 million pro forma. Net leverage on house-adjusted EBITDA, which deducts master lease rent from the issuer's Adjusted EBITDAR, is 1.97x, and Financial foundation states no pro forma figure on that basis. The ratios use carrying-value debt and exclude operating lease liabilities, and the covenant maximum of 4.50x is defined on a lender basis that the filings do not print, so covenant headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1

Cash flow no longer covers the spending programme. Operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 left a shortfall of USD 142.6 million after capital expenditures of USD 456.0 million, and the trailing twelve months show a shortfall of USD 15.7 million against free cash flow of USD 388.5 million in 2025. The USD 364.2 million paid for tax credits bought in 2025 more than explains the gap; without it nine-month free cash flow would have been USD 221.6 million and cash conversion 87.1% of trailing EBITDA instead of 53.8%. After shareholder returns of USD 518.4 million the nine-month shortfall was USD 661.0 million, met largely by net facility borrowings of USD 625.9 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 58–59; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B3

Earnings are eroding faster than revenue, but the third quarter shows stabilisation. Revenue is flat at USD 3,022.2 million for nine months, yet house-adjusted EBITDA on trailing revenue fell from 32.5% in 2024 to 29.6%, as market access fees fell away and the earnings of Las Vegas Locals and Downtown Las Vegas declined 5.7% and 13.8% in nine months. In the third quarter alone total Adjusted EBITDAR was down 0.7%, with Online earnings up 16.0% as the fee change laps, while Downtown Las Vegas fell 20.5% and Las Vegas Locals 5.1%. Operating income fell USD 22.4 million as depreciation rose USD 65.4 million, which does not reduce EBITDA but does reduce earnings available after reinvestment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44, 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B4; calculation B5; calculation B6

Refinancing is the main credit event and it falls in one window. USD 1,800.9 million of principal, 66.7% of the total, matures in 2027: the facility at its springing maturity of 2027-09-01 and the notes due 2027-12-01, so all USD 800.9 million drawn is classified as current. Committed availability of USD 1,834.9 million covers it only if the term loan is used: USD 800.0 million is a delayed-draw term loan that can be drawn only until 2027-07-01, and revolver availability of USD 1,034.9 million alone would leave USD 34.9 million after retiring the USD 1,000.0 million notes. The issuer states that availability suffices to retire the notes; doing so lifts the floating-rate share of debt from 29.7% to 66.7% and each 100 bp of interest-rate change would cost USD 18.0 million a year against USD 8.0 million today.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 61, 67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B7; calculation B8

Interest cover is high but flattered by timing. Trailing cash interest of USD 111.7 million, which gives cover of 9.79x, includes only quarters after the 2025 repayment, when the facility balance was lower than the USD 800.9 million now drawn. Annualising the third-quarter interest expense of USD 32.5 million gives USD 130.0 million and cover of 8.42x, and retiring the 2027 notes with facility draws at 5.1% would lift annual interest to about USD 133.7 million and cover to 8.18x. Cover remains adequate but is falling as facility borrowing grows, and it would fall further if the facility replaced the fixed-rate notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 55, 61; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B9

Financial policy is the swing factor, and a family-influenced board sets it. Shareholder returns of USD 518.4 million were 1.65x operating cash flow, the share count fell 6.7% from the end of 2025 to the end of September, and USD 387.1 million of repurchase authorization remains, limited only by restricted-payment terms whose size the filings do not state. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium: no sponsor and an unqualified audit, offset by this pace of distributions. Creditors should read the 2026 pace as policy that the board can reverse in one quarter, which is both the risk and the mitigant.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 27, 63; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B3

Structure and claims outside the debt figure matter for priority. The credit facility is secured on substantially all assets other than gaming licenses and could be effectively senior to other debt to the extent of collateral value, while the notes due 2027 and 2031 are unsecured and guaranteed by wholly owned subsidiaries. Undiscounted master lease payments were USD 537.1 million at the end of 2025 and master lease rent was USD 86.4 million in nine months, and the Norfolk project adds USD 750.0 million of spending with USD 275.0 million in 2026. Legal priority and recovery are not assessed here.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 26, 62, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12

Business risk is moderate and competition is stated but not measured. The company competes with other casino operators, Native American casinos that in some cases pay lower or no taxes, online operators and lotteries, and gaming regulation and taxation can change by state. Midwest and South properties produce 56.7% of segment earnings and no segment exceeds 60%, which limits dependence on one market, but the filings give no market share, customer concentration or peer comparison, so the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is that the 2026 cash gap is mostly one-off and reversible. Without the USD 364.2 million tax-credit payment nine-month free cash flow would have been USD 221.6 million, third-quarter Adjusted EBITDAR was down only 0.7%, the issuer states that availability can retire the notes due 2027, and repurchases and growth spending can be cut: maintenance spending is about USD 250.0 million of a USD 650.0 million plan and USD 325.0 million of the plan is growth and Norfolk. That case wins if repurchases slow after the 2027 notes are addressed, if third-quarter stabilisation holds and if the term loan is drawn or the notes refinanced before 2027-07-01.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 48, 64; calculation B2; calculation B5; calculation B10

The case for a worse view wins if repurchases continue at the 2026 pace while the facility stays drawn, if Las Vegas Locals and Downtown Las Vegas keep falling, or if Norfolk costs exceed USD 750.0 million. A downside in which those two segments lose 10% of fiscal 2025 earnings and the remaining USD 387.1 million authorization is spent on borrowing takes net leverage to 2.65x and leaves USD 447.8 million of committed availability after the notes are retired; that is not distress, but it is thin liquidity just before the springing maturity. The executed credit agreement, the indentures and a refinancing of the notes due 2027 would each move the view.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B11
### Limitations

- No management projection, refinancing plan or term loan drawing plan was supplied, so the downside scenario is a sensitivity built from reported figures and stated assumptions; it shows direction and order of magnitude and cannot show the actual path of liquidity before the springing maturity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation B11

- Run-rate interest and refinancing cost rest on the third-quarter interest expense and the stated blended facility rate, and the terms of any 2027 refinancing are unknown, so cover after refinancing may be higher or lower than shown.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 61; calculation B9

- No peer, sector or rating-agency evidence was supplied, so the competitive position and the business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers rest on the company's own descriptions and are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14

- Customer concentration, seasonality and slot hold volatility are not stated, so the revenue durability judgement rests on the direction of reported volumes and margins, and a view on within-year cash needs is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strengths are, in order, the spread of earnings, moderate leverage with high cover, committed liquidity, the discretion over spending and an audited public-company structure. Earnings come from properties in 11 states and Midwest and South properties provide 56.7% of segment earnings, so a shock in Las Vegas does not remove most of the cash flow. Net leverage of 2.17x, 2.19x pro forma, and cover of 9.79x give room to absorb a lower EBITDA or higher interest cost. Committed availability of USD 1,834.9 million funds the 2027 maturities if the term loan is drawn in time. Repurchases and USD 325.0 million of growth and Norfolk spending can be cut. The company is publicly held with an unqualified audit opinion and no related-party leakage beyond compensation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 48, 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B4; calculation B7; calculation B10

The weaknesses are, in order, the shareholder-return pace, the 2027 refinancing window, eroding Las Vegas earnings, negative free cash flow and fixed charges outside debt. Returns of USD 518.4 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 313.4 million and facility principal rose USD 640.2 million, which rebuilds leverage. The facility's springing maturity and the notes due 2027 concentrate USD 1,800.9 million in one year, with USD 800.0 million of availability expiring on 2027-07-01. Las Vegas Locals earnings fell 5.7% and Downtown Las Vegas 13.8% in nine months, lowering house-adjusted margin to 29.6%. Trailing free cash flow is a shortfall of USD 15.7 million. Master lease rent of USD 86.4 million and Norfolk spending of USD 275.0 million in 2026 rank ahead of or compete with debt service.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 20–21, 25–26; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B7

### Company description

Boyd Gaming operates 26 gaming properties in 11 states, the online business Boyd Interactive and, under a management agreement, the Sky River Casino. Gaming is 65.8% of revenue and the filings call most revenue cash-based, which supports short cash cycles; the loyalty programme, Boyd Rewards, links the properties and the online offer. The business is discretionary and location-driven, so durability depends on visits and spending. For creditors this supports visibility of cash flow and liquidity preservation in a downturn, while the lack of any disclosed customer concentration or market share leaves refinancing confidence resting on the earnings record.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 41, 45; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly held with the Chairman and her immediate family owning about 30% of the shares and directors and executive officers about 31%, and it has no sponsor. The guarantors of the notes and the credit facility are wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, while the Norfolk entity is a consolidated variable interest entity tied to a tribal gaming authority, with a company option over a percentage of its membership interests that the filings do not size, and the Sky River Casino is managed under an agreement with Wilton Rancheria. The notes and facility therefore sit at the parent and guarantor level, and the filings do not state whether cash at those projects is available to the borrower group. Dividends and repurchases are limited by restricted-payment terms that are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26, 62; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mostly slot-driven gaming volume and win, plus rooms, food and beverage and online fees; revenue is not contracted, so it is discretionary and visit-based. Gaming revenue rose 1.1% in nine months on slot win up 1.7% and slot handle up 0.8%, room revenue fell 3.2% on a 1.8% lower average daily rate, and online reimbursements of USD 383.0 million carry no margin. Pricing power is limited in the locals and regional markets, so revenue durability rests on volumes: flat revenue of USD 3,022.2 million with falling Las Vegas earnings means durability is adequate rather than growing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 45–47; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B4
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Property costs include fixed elements such as master lease rent of USD 86.4 million in nine months, so a revenue shortfall can flow quickly into earnings: gaming margin fell to 60.5% from 61.1%, room margin to 57.9% from 59.8% and corporate expense rose to USD 76.7 million from USD 71.4 million. House-adjusted EBITDA margin on trailing revenue is 29.6% against 32.5% in 2024. Margins can be defended only with cost action; the filings describe no cost programme, so margin pressure is a live downside.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 45–47, 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B4
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is high: maintenance spending is about USD 250.0 million a year, with USD 75.0 million for hotel renovation, USD 50.0 million of growth projects and USD 275.0 million for Norfolk in 2026, a USD 650.0 million plan of which USD 456.0 million was spent in nine months. Cash conversion of trailing EBITDA fell from 92.9% in 2025 to 53.8%, or 87.1% without the tax-credit payment. Capex is flexible beyond maintenance, so free cash flow can recover if growth spending is paused, but Norfolk is committed until it opens in November 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B10
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is the force that matters: properties compete with other operators in each state and in adjacent states, and expansion by competitors or new openings could reduce volumes. Licensing requirements limit new entrants, but Native American casinos and online operators already compete, and some competitors pay lower or no taxes. Substitutes include online gaming and lotteries; buyer power looks high because customers can choose among nearby casinos and the filings describe loyalty rewards as the retention tool; supplier power is not a stated credit factor. The net effect is limited pricing power and margin pressure rather than a collapse in volumes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 27
### PEST factors

Regulation and tax are the only PEST factors that materially affect credit: gaming licenses require continued suitability, tax changes and proposals for a federal tax on casino revenues could reduce earnings, and licenses are excluded from the collateral of the credit facility. Macroeconomic, social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials, beyond the visit and spending sensitivity already described.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 23
### SWOT

Strengths are the spread of earnings across 11 states, moderate leverage, committed liquidity and discretion over spending. Weaknesses are shareholder returns above cash generation, the 2027 maturity concentration and falling Las Vegas earnings. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the opening of Norfolk in November 2027, the Cadence Crossing replacement of Jokers Wild and Boyd Interactive revenue growth of USD 14.2 million. Threats that could weaken it are a Las Vegas locals downturn, a failed or costly refinancing of the notes due 2027, a Norfolk cost overrun and tax or regulatory change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 43, 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

On a ratings-style lens the profile is adequate: leverage is moderate at 2.17x (2.19x pro forma), cover is 9.79x and falling to 8.42x on a run-rate basis, liquidity is committed but time-limited, access to markets is demonstrated by the 2019 and 2021 note issues and the January 2026 facility, and financial policy is the weakest dimension. The trend is up for leverage and down for cash conversion. Missing datapoints are the covenant ratios, the lender definition of EBITDA and the restricted-payment capacity.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, pages 116–117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B9
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next 12 to 24 months the headwinds are the refinancing window to 2027-09-01, higher floating-rate exposure, lower market access fees and Las Vegas weakness; tailwinds are third-quarter stabilisation, the lapping of the online fee change, the Norfolk opening in November 2027 and discretionary capital spending. Over three to five years the 2031 notes of USD 900.0 million are the next maturity and the master leases run to 2031-04-30; the filings give no sector forecast or management projection, so the medium-term outlook is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_byd_bgc20251121-10k.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 47–48; calculation B5; calculation B7
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a Las Vegas locals downturn in which Las Vegas Locals and Downtown Las Vegas lose 10% of fiscal 2025 earnings, a loss of USD 50.1 million, while the board spends the remaining USD 387.1 million repurchase authorization on facility borrowing. The first operating break is lower gaming volume against fixed property costs and master lease rent, which cuts trailing reported EBITDA to USD 1,044.0 million. Net leverage rises from 2.17x to 2.28x on the earnings loss alone and to 2.65x with the borrowing; retiring the notes due 2027 with facility draws leaves USD 447.8 million of committed availability, interest rises to about USD 154.8 million and cover falls to 6.75x. Management levers are stopping repurchases, deferring growth spending of USD 325.0 million and drawing the term loan before 2027-07-01. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but only if the term loan is drawn or the notes are refinanced before its availability lapses.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_byd_bgc20260930-10q.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 27, 61; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B11
### Overall credit view

Overall, Boyd Gaming presents an adequate business profile supported by earnings spread across 11 states, moderate leverage and committed liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by a shareholder-return pace above cash generation and a concentrated 2027 refinancing. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: conversion of EBITDA to operating cash flow was 92.9% in 2025 and 87.1% in the trailing year before the tax-credit payment. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on drawing the term loan or refinancing the notes before 2027-07-01 and on the board holding back repurchases. The primary downside path is weaker Las Vegas locals earnings combined with continued repurchases. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the indentures, the proxy statement and a management refinancing plan. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: the 2027 refinancing window.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B7; calculation B11
